Once parked, it never takes the real outcome.\\nScenario: For a refinement, the expiry branch calls \\u0060RecordEndAsync\\u0060 with \\u0060DispatchExpired\\u0060, which appends \\u0060PlanDecider.ParkOn(... SessionFailed, S1)\\u0060 to the plan in the same save. For a challenge, the next plan step on the expiring node reads \\u0060task.LatestChallengeOutcome\\u0060 as the expiry (\\u0060PlanEngine.cs:284-296\\u0060) and appends \\u0060AfterChallenge\\u0060, which parks with \\u0060ChallengeFailed\\u0060. \\u0060PlanDraftState.Apply(PlanParked)\\u0060 clears \\u0060RunningSessionId\\u0060 and \\u0060ChallengeRequestedAt\\u0060, and \\u0060Apply(PlanDraftMoved)\\u0060 never clears \\u0060ParkReason\\u0060. So in either delivery order the plan ends up parked on every node, even after the real verdict or refinement outcome lands and the task view shows it. If node A had already moved on and dispatched a next session S2, the replicated park also clears the plan\\u0027s \\u0060RunningSessionId\\u0060, so \\u0060PlanOfAsync\\u0060 cannot match S2\\u0027s outcome to the plan. The settle period makes this rarer, but whenever the outcome arrives after ceiling plus settle, the plan stays parked until a person resumes it.
